newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan dealer to sell GM's Saab cars in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan dealer to sell GM's Saab cars in July.

text.p: Yanase & Co Ltd, a leading foreign car dealer, said on Thursday it would start selling cars made by Saab Automobile AB, the Swedish unit of General Motors Corp (GM), in Japan on July 1.

Asked if Yanase had a sales target for Saab cars, Yanase president Takahide Inayama said: "We want to start with an annual sales target of between 2,800 and 3,000 cars for next year. That will exceed Saab's best sales volume in the past."
GM and Sweden's AB Investor each own 50 percent of Saab Automobile. Yanase has been selling GM's U.S.-made cars in Japan since 1915.
Saabs will be sold in Japan through Yanase's 185 sales outlets for GM cars.
Saab plans to launch and market the 95 model in Japan around the end of this year, said Sakari Ryopponen, Saab Automobile's market area director for Asia Pacific and the Middle East.
Saab plans to increase global sales from the current 100,000 units to 150,000 units in the next three years, he said.

In October last year, Saab Automobile started to market and service its cars by itself in Japan after cancelling its sales tie-up with Mizwa International, a unit of Mizwa Motor Co Ltd, the sole agent in Japan for Porsche PSHG.F cars.
Sales of Saab cars in Japan totalled 901 cars in 1996, down 33.4 percent from a year earlier.
Yanase has been selling GM's Adam Opel cars in Japan since January 1993. Through Yanase's vast network, Japanese sales of Opel cars jumped to 38,339 cars in 1996, up 18 percent from a year earlier.

Asked about the prospects for import car demand in Japan, Douglas Herberger, the president of General Motors Japan Ltd, the Japanese unit of General Motors Corp, said: "We currently regard prospects for growth for the entire 1997 import (car) market to be very modest."
